content:
The new Apple TV 4K was long overdue and was originally expected to launch last fall. However, with Siri AI finally ready, all signs point to a new Apple TV 4K making its debut—possibly at the September 9 event. Here's what the rumours say so far.

#1: Siri Remote update

While no details have been revealed yet, Apple is reportedly set to release an updated version of the Siri Remote for the new Apple TV 4K.

Code from one version of macOS 26.7 appears to have confirmed the existence of a new Siri Remote. And before that leak, Mark Gurman had reported that the new hardware could come with an "improved Apple TV Remote".

It doesn't sound like much will change, but hopefully at least a second-generation ultra-wideband chip will be added to support Precision Finding.

#2: Siri AI and more Apple Intelligence features

Siri AI is expected to be the main marketing focus for the new Apple TV and other new Home products.

Apple has yet to announce whether the new assistant will come to Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But there are indications that tvOS 27 will add Siri AI—and likely only support the new hardware.

There's also a good chance other Apple Intelligence features, such as a more powerful search experience, will be added.

#3: Brand new A-series chip

The current Apple TV features the A15 Bionic chip that first appeared in 2021. The new model is expected to see a massive performance boost.

It will use a more powerful, brand new A-series chip and support various AI features.

There are rumours it could be the A17 Pro or A18 chip, but most of those reports came before the Siri AI announcement. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple opted for the even more powerful A19 or A20 chip instead.

#4: N1 wireless chip

Top comment by Wade Burris

I hope the remote can get Precision Find My and a sound cue to find it. Also hoping the harder edges of the remote can be improved.

Additionally, welcome would be more alignment with CarPlay, like replying to messages and using widgets. If iMessage notifications could pop up on the screen, that would be a very useful feature for me. I live alone, so there are no privacy concerns.

The N1 wireless chip, reportedly first adopted in the iPhone 17, is also expected to be used in the new Apple TV 4K.

With the N1 chip, the Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and support Thread networking.

By comparison, the current Apple TV hardware, which has been out for four years, only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features do you want to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
